concerns.concern: The manuscript ignores the established literature on current-driven, electrically writable and erasable metastable high-J_c vortex states in conventional superconductors such as NbSe₂ and CeRu₂. Those states closely match the reported behaviour, so the claims of novelty and of an origin in the superconducting order are overstated.
concerns.quote: History-dependent, electrically writable and erasable high-J_c states are a well-documented phenomenon in vortex matter, most prominently near the peak effect in 2H-NbSe₂ and CeRu₂.

concerns.concern: The data do not show what distinguishes the effect from generic order–disorder metastability of a single vortex species, including edge contamination via surface barriers. The reviewer asks for discriminating tests: field-cooled vs zero-field-cooled, sample geometry/contact layout, ac shaking, and comparison with any peak effect.
concerns.quote: The authors should explain what in their data distinguishes the UTe₂ effect from a generic order–disorder metastability of a single vortex species.

concerns.concern: Joule heating at the spot-welded contacts (roughly 0.2–2 mW) is not excluded, and a mixing-chamber thermometer cannot detect millisecond transients. Contact resistances, a time-resolved sample-temperature estimate, thermal time constants and a heater-pulse control without transport current are needed.
concerns.quote: Joule heating, and specifically a thermal-quench mechanism, is not excluded.

concerns.concern: The dependence on turn-off rate is exactly what a heat-then-quench mechanism predicts, since faster turn-off means faster cooling. The total-energy argument therefore does not discriminate against heating.
concerns.quote: The observed dependence on α (Fig. 2c, ED Fig. 1c) is exactly what thermal quenching would predict.

concerns.concern: The argument that heating would show up everywhere fails. A heating-induced metastable vortex state would only appear where vortex matter can be metastable.
concerns.quote: The argument that heating would appear everywhere fails if the consequence of heating, a metastable vortex state, exists only where vortex matter is metastable.

concerns.concern: The correspondence of the memory region with SC1/SC2 coexistence is contradicted in sample S2. There the effect peaks near 10 T and is gone by 15–16 T, below the claimed boundary, contrary to the text's statement that it persists until just below 20 T.
concerns.quote: The text's statement that the effect persists "until the phase boundary out of SC1 into SC2 is crossed", "just below 20 T" for S2, is not what ED Fig. 8 shows.

concerns.concern: The field windows of S1 and S2 differ by about a factor of two, and this is attributed to crystal quality without any independent determination of the SC1/SC2 boundary. The reviewer requests a thermodynamic or susceptibility measurement of the boundary on the measured crystals.
concerns.quote: This is attributed to crystal quality, with no independent determination of the SC1/SC2 boundary in either crystal.

concerns.concern: The memory field window is the same at θ = 0° and 15°, although the phase boundary should move with angle. The claimed angular tracking of the boundary rests on a single field and a single equilibrium trace, so onset/offset versus θ at several fields is needed.
concerns.quote: The angular argument rests on a single field (15 T, Fig. 4f) and a single equilibrium V(θ) trace (Fig. 4g).

concerns.concern: At 29 T and beyond 20°, J_c is nearly zero and V(J) is nearly ohmic. The absence of memory there is therefore uninformative as evidence for a phase-specific effect.
concerns.quote: At 29 T and θ ≳ 20° (ED Fig. 10), J_c is nearly zero and V(J) is close to ohmic. Absence of memory there says little.

concerns.concern: The abrupt versus smooth protocols are not properly specified. The text claims dc excitation, but pulse-delta mode was used, so a 'smooth' sweep may itself consist of many abrupt drops to zero. It is unclear which waveform feature writes and which erases.
concerns.quote: If the low level is zero, every "smooth" sweep consists of many abrupt drops to zero.

concerns.concern: The shortest pulses and fastest ramps are comparable to the current source's settling time and waveform resolution, and lead inductance or capacitance may distort them. The actual current waveforms are unverified, and oscilloscope traces and full pulse parameters are requested.
concerns.quote: These are comparable to the output settling of the 6221 and to the time resolution of a 100-point arbitrary waveform.

concerns.concern: In Fig. 1d,e the erase is drawn as a rectangular block followed by an abrupt step to the probe level. This contradicts the statement that erasure requires a smooth ramp-down.
concerns.quote: This conflicts with the statement that erasure requires smooth ramp-down.

concerns.concern: The claims of retention for 'at least several hours' and of non-volatility are unsupported: the longest time series is about 400 s. Long-time V(t) or ΔJ creep data are needed.
concerns.quote: No retention data appear. The longest time series is ~400 s (Fig. 1d).

concerns.concern: Endurance is not characterised. There are only five write/erase cycles, and the two readout levels differ by only about 0.5 µV, so many more cycles with level distributions are requested.
concerns.quote: many more write/erase cycles than the five in Fig. 1d, with the distribution of the two read-out levels

concerns.concern: Read-disturb is not tested. Reading the '0' state requires a current above the equilibrium J_c, so a probe that ends abruptly could itself write the state.
concerns.quote: Reading the "0" state requires J above the equilibrium J_c, so a probe ending abruptly could itself act as a pump.

concerns.concern: The description of the state's lifetime is inconsistent. It is called 'metastable' or a 'long-lived transient' in places but 'not transiently metastable' elsewhere.
concerns.quote: the abstract and Methods say "metastable" or "long-lived transient", while p. 7 says "does not appear to be transiently metastable".

concerns.concern: The RSJ model has many hand-chosen parameters, some unreported, picked so that the π minimum has the higher J_c and viscosity. Reproducing hysteresis is therefore largely by construction, and the model should either reproduce the dependences without retuning or be presented as a toy model, softening 'we confirm'.
concerns.quote: Reproducing a hysteretic loop (Fig. 3c, ED Fig. 2) is therefore largely by construction.

concerns.concern: The binary two-minimum model cannot explain the observed continuous, saturating dependence of ΔJ on amplitude, duration and rate, or the amplitude threshold near 3 A cm⁻².
concerns.quote: The model is binary: the pump always lands at φ = π. The experiment shows a continuous, saturating dependence of ΔJ

concerns.concern: The text conflates flux-flow damping/resistance with critical current, whereas in an RSJ model J_c is set by the potential gradient. The memory and equilibrium curves also converge at high J, showing no change in flux-flow slope.
concerns.quote: In an RSJ model J_c is set by max U′, not by γ.

concerns.concern: The claim that unbroken inversion symmetry forces the second minimum to φ = π, identified with SC1/SC2 domain walls, is not justified. Mapping a single phase variable onto a mm-scale bulk vortex ensemble is asserted rather than argued.
concerns.quote: The claim that unbroken inversion symmetry forces the second minimum to φ = π, identified with SC1/SC2 domain walls, needs justification.

concerns.concern: Treating the damping γ as a proxy for injected current when plotting J–V in the model is unexplained.
concerns.quote: The statement that γ is treated "as a proxy to the injected current J" when plotting J–V needs explanation.

concerns.concern: ΔJ values for the same sample, field and temperature vary from about 0.05 to 0.55 A cm⁻² across figures, and no plot has error bars. A uniform ΔJ definition, repeated trials with standard deviations, and the field-ramp history are requested.
concerns.quote: No error bars are shown in any ΔJ plot.

concerns.concern: Different tuning knobs saturate at different ΔJ values. This suggests a continuum of states rather than the model's two minima, and should be discussed.
concerns.quote: It suggests a continuum of states rather than the two minima of the model, and deserves discussion.

concerns.concern: The decrease of ΔJ with temperature may simply track the decrease of J_c, so ΔJ/J_c should be shown. Warming may also shift the sample relative to the SC1/SC2 boundary.
concerns.quote: ΔJ is not normalised by J_c(T). A decrease of ΔJ with T may simply track the decrease of J_c.

concerns.concern: The stronger effect at low temperature does not support an 'intrinsic' origin. The diode-effect analogy is unconvincing, because glassy pinning metastability is generically strongest at low T.
concerns.quote: Glassy pinning metastability is generically strongest at low T, where thermal activation cannot anneal.

concerns.concern: Calling the effect 'intrinsic' conflicts with the pinning-dependent mechanism and the strong sample dependence. 'Intrinsic' should be defined, and more samples across RRR (including S3 with the dc protocol) and current directions should be measured.
concerns.quote: "Intrinsic" sits uneasily with the proposed mechanism, which is pinning-dependent, and with the strong sample dependence (S1 vs S2).

concerns.concern: Current densities are nominal for spot-welded surface contacts. Sample dimensions and the possible non-uniformity of the current distribution should be reported.
concerns.quote: J is quoted as nominal for spot-welded contacts on the (001) surface. Report sample dimensions and comment on current-distribution non-uniformity.

concerns.concern: The polarity dependence is not quantified, and at the slow rates used the signal is weak and the enhancement is not visually evident. ΔJ for both polarities in the strong-rate regime is requested, since a symmetric enhancement would argue against Bean-type remanence.
concerns.quote: ED Fig. 4 is described as "consistent" for both probe polarities, but the effect is not quantified.

concerns.concern: The statement that the Bean critical-state model depends only on total imparted energy mischaracterises that model and should be revised.
concerns.quote: The Bean-model statement on p. 13 ("depending only on the total energy imparted") mischaracterises the critical-state model and should be revised.

concerns.concern: The angular falloff of ΔJ is gradual rather than 'abrupt', and the equilibrium J_c also decreases with angle. ΔJ/J_c versus θ and angular data at other fields are requested.
concerns.quote: Fig. 4f at 15 T shows ΔJ falling gradually from ~0.1 at 0–5° to ~0 at 20°, not "abruptly".

concerns.concern: The ~1 nW power figure covers only reading, which is itself resistive. It omits write and erase energy and time (µW for ms; a 20 s erase ramp) and contact dissipation.
concerns.quote: The ~1 nW figure refers only to reading. Reading the "0" state is resistive (flux flow).

concerns.concern: The application claims do not acknowledge that operation requires 7–20 T and temperatures below 0.6 K.
concerns.quote: Operation requires 7–20 T and T < 0.6 K.

concerns.concern: Scaling to ≲1 pW assumes the same vortex physics holds in µm-scale devices, where edge effects would dominate.
concerns.quote: The scaling to ≲1 pW assumes the same vortex physics in µm-scale devices, where edge effects would dominate.

concerns.concern: Ref. 59, on intrinsic carrier concentration in silicon, does not support the power comparison with silicon memory.
concerns.quote: Ref. 59, on intrinsic carrier concentration in silicon, does not support the comparison with silicon memory power.

concerns.concern: No direct probe of the proposed quenched vortex disorder is provided. Flux-flow noise, SANS or scanning Hall/SQUID measurements could discriminate the two-vortex-species picture from single-species metastability.
concerns.quote: Seek a direct probe of the proposed quenched vortex disorder in the two states, such as broadband flux-flow noise, SANS, or scanning Hall/SQUID

concerns.concern: There is no direct structural evidence that the equilibrium vortex state is 'highly ordered'.
concerns.quote: There is no direct structural evidence that the equilibrium state is "highly ordered".

concerns.concern: The schematic phase diagrams should be replaced with data points. Fig. 1a colours the memory region up to ~1 K, although the data show it gone by 0.6 K.
concerns.quote: Fig. 1a currently colours the memory region up to ~1 K, whereas the data show it gone by 0.6 K.

concerns.concern: The text says Fig. 3 covers 50 mK–1.0 K, but the heatmaps stop at 0.6 K and the 1.0 K trace comes from a different sample and field. The sample and field for each panel should be stated.
concerns.quote: The text says Fig. 3 covers 50 mK–1.0 K, but the heatmaps stop at 0.6 K and the 1.0 K trace is from S1 at 20 T.

concerns.concern: The Fig. 1b caption describes the erase as a sweep from a large negative value, while Methods describes 40 → 0 mA. The polarity for each dataset should be stated.
concerns.quote: The Fig. 1b caption describes the erase as a sweep from a large negative value, whereas Methods describes 40 → 0 mA.

concerns.concern: The role of Fig. 4h (sample S3, ac measurement, no memory protocol) in the argument is unclear. It should be connected to the memory region or moved to the SI.
concerns.quote: The role of Fig. 4h (S3, ac, 400 mK, resistive magnet) in the argument is unclear, because no memory protocol was applied.

concerns.concern: The raw datasets are not yet available and should be provided for review.
concerns.quote: Datasets "will be uploaded … prior to publication". Please make them available for review.

concerns.concern: 'Minimise entropy' should read 'free energy'.
concerns.quote: "minimise entropy" (p. 13) should be "free energy".

concerns.concern: The phrase about pinning forces between vortices conflates vortex–vortex interactions with vortex–defect pinning.
concerns.quote: "stronger pinning forces between vortices" conflates vortex–vortex interactions with vortex–defect pinning.

concerns.concern: The analogy to supercurrent rectification by the superconducting diode effect in the Fig. 1d caption is loose and should be removed.
concerns.quote: The phrase "akin to supercurrent rectification by the superconducting diode effect" (Fig. 1d caption) is a loose analogy. Consider removing it.

concerns.concern: There are several typos and unit errors: φ written as π in Methods, a wrong axis unit in ED Fig. 1a, inconsistent α units in ED Fig. 5b, J_ext in Fig. 3b, and the tuning wording on p. 9.
concerns.quote: Methods: "global minimum at π = 0" should read φ = 0.

concerns.concern: Refs. 26 and 57 are duplicates, and the page numbers in ref. 31 should be checked.
concerns.quote: Refs. 26 and 57 are duplicates. Check the page numbers in ref. 31.
